- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes, especially after sentiment turns positive (e.g., +0.40 or +0.80) — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such sentiment shifts.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >40), model tends to overcorrect downward — apply a “lag correction” by holding forecast at 1–2 days above true value to avoid premature drop.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.50 or below), model underreacts — increase forecast baseline by 1–3% to account for suppressed volatility.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-predicts decline after recent rise — if true outcome shows sustained upward trend, delay downward correction by 1–2 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture “late-cycle” momentum — if sentiment is positive and price is rising, add 1–3% to forecast for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model tends to forecast flat — if true outcome shows upward movement, add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
